questions.q: What must happen to a data source before Microsoft Purview can scan it?
options: It must be classified manually
It must be assigned a sensitivity label
It must be registered, giving Purview its address and mapping it to a collection
It must be added to a glossary term
questions.explain: Registration gives the Data Map the source's address (account, subscription, connection details) and maps it to a collection or domain — only after that can a scan be configured.

questions.q: Which permissions are needed to register and manage a data source?
options: The Data Source Admin role, plus another Data Map role such as Data Reader, at the relevant collection
Global Administrator on the Azure tenant
No special permissions are required
Only the Policy Author role
questions.explain: Registering and managing a source requires the Data Source Admin role plus one of the other Data Map roles (such as Data Reader), assigned at the collection or a parent collection.

questions.q: What is the difference between Map view and Table view for registered data sources?
options: Map view is only for Azure sources; Table view is for all other sources
Table view shows scan results; Map view shows classifications
There is no difference — they show the same information identically
Map view shows domains and collections as a visual hierarchy; Table view is a flat, sortable list
questions.explain: Map view visualizes the domain/collection hierarchy with sources nested inside it, while Table view is a flat sortable list — better once you have many sources.

questions.q: When you move a registered source to a different collection, what happens to assets that were already scanned into the old collection?
options: They move immediately along with the source
They stay in their original collection until the next scan runs, then they move too
They are deleted and must be rescanned from scratch
They are duplicated into both collections permanently
questions.explain: Scans move with the source automatically, but already-scanned assets remain in their original collection until the next scan runs — only then do they move to the new collection.

questions.q: Which of these data source connections can NOT be moved between collections?
options: A single Azure Blob Storage account
A single PostgreSQL database
A single Azure SQL Database
Multi-source connections like Azure (Multiple), AWS account (Multiple), and Azure Synapse Analytics (Multiple)
questions.explain: Data source connections that register multiple sources at once — Azure (Multiple), AWS account (Multiple), and Azure Synapse Analytics (Multiple) — can't be moved between collections.
